sections.h2: Where to pay in Yadkin County
sections.html:
The Yadkin County Tax Department is in Yadkinville. The in-person payment counter is in the Magnolia building across from the courthouse at 101 South State Street, and the office line is 336-849-7903. The tax office page has the rest.

There are four ways to pay:

  • Online, through the county's bill lookup and payment site.
  • By telephone at 866-249-4184, with the year and bill number.
  • In person at the Magnolia building.
  • By mail to Yadkin County Tax Department, P.O. Box 1217, Yadkinville NC 27055, with a printed copy of the online bill.

Contact the office for address changes, value changes and general questions. Deed work belongs with an attorney.

sections.h2: Yadkin County housing at a glance
sections.html:
Yadkinville is the county seat, and the tax counter sits there. Most sellers will deal with the office by phone first, then visit the Magnolia building only if a payment or form has to be handed over in person. The county covers roughly 335 square miles of land, with about 111 residents on each. The 2025 population estimate is 38,325, a 3.0% gain over 2020.

  • Owners occupy 76.9% of homes.
  • The typical owned home is valued at $181,200, and typical rent is $766.
  • About 22.4% of residents are 65 or older, so age-based relief matters here.

Only 116 building permits were issued in 2025, so new construction is modest and resale homes dominate. Many households stay in place, which means a lot of owners have not seen a recent sale price on their own house.

A 2027 revaluation is underway. State law keeps every county on a cycle of at most eight years, and the 2023 reappraisal notices are posted in the county's document center.

Revaluation moves each parcel's assessed value to its market value as of the new January 1 date. State law defines true value as the price a willing buyer and willing seller would agree on. Owners often see bigger changes than usual in a reappraisal year, and the review window is the time to compare the new notice with recent nearby sales.

Ask the tax office when notices will be mailed and how to reach an appraiser. Once a new notice arrives, set it beside the 2023 value and beside what similar Yadkinville and rural houses recently sold for, and note any change that looks out of line. The county keeps a reappraisal appeal form in its online form center.

The county offers a 2% discount for paying in August, ahead of the September 1 due date. Interest starts after the grace period that ends the day before January 6.

Solid waste fees are billed separately: $76.00 per household, $38.00 for a household with the elderly exemption, and $10.00 for extra stickers. They are not part of the value-based tax, so ask whether they are paid up at closing. The bill goes to whoever held title at the start of the year, so a seller who closes in the fall still owes the tax for that year unless the settlement statement shifts it.

Your first move is a phone call or email to the tax office, since it handles value changes. A failed informal request goes to the county's review board as a formal appeal. The commissioners usually serve as that board.

A hearing can be requested in writing or in person before the board adjourns. Its decision is mailed within 30 days after it adjourns. In a reappraisal year the board calendar runs longer, so ask which dates apply. A stronger case includes recent sale prices of similar homes nearby, photographs and repair estimates.

Beyond the county, the Property Tax Commission takes a written notice filed within 30 days of the mailed decision.

The Yadkin tax office takes applications for state exemptions and exclusions. The three below use NCDOR's 2026 figures. An owner picks one, because they cannot be combined.

North Carolina relief programs open to Yadkin County owners
ProgramQualificationBenefit
Elderly or disabled exclusionAge 65 plus or fully and permanently disabled, income no higher than $38,800 for 2026Greater of $25,000 or 50% of value excluded
Disabled veteran exclusionA qualifying disabled veteran or unmarried surviving spouse, no age or income testFirst $45,000 of value excluded
Circuit breakerSame age or disability test, five years living in the home, income up to $58,200Tax capped at 4% or 5% of income, excess deferred

File Form AV-9 with the county assessor, which accepts it through June 1.

The tax office has three email links: one for assessor and payment matters, one for appraisal, and one for exemptions. Pick the link that matches your question. Use the appraisal link for a value question and the exemptions link for relief forms, so the message reaches the right person quickly.

You can also pull printable parcel maps from the county's GIS site and download property record cards from the tax page. The record card lists what the county has recorded about a house, so read it for errors in square footage or condition before a buyer's appraiser does. Deed questions belong with an attorney and the Register of Deeds.

Settlement takes the balance from the seller's side. The lien is dated to the first of the year, so a sale does not wipe it out, and an unpaid parcel can be collected through a courthouse auction.

Request a payoff amount that includes solid waste fees before you list, and pass it along to the closing attorney. The payoff should be dated close to closing, since interest keeps adding to a late balance every month. Rural land can carry extra layers, so ask for the whole parcel record.

sections.h2: Solid waste fees and business listing
sections.html:
Count the $76.00 household fee among the yearly carrying costs of a Yadkin property. A purchaser's lawyer may want proof that stickers and fees are current, so check with the tax office.

Business personal property, such as tools or equipment kept at a rental or workshop, is listed in January. The listing period runs from the first working day of January through its end, and commissioners may extend it. Anyone with good cause may request more time in writing. Anything not listed can draw a penalty, so ask the office how to list.

Sellers in Yadkin County do best when they plan backward from the first day of September. A seller who plans a fall or winter closing should confirm the bill status in August, when the 2% discount applies, and again before the end of the year.

  • January 1: ownership and value fixed for the year
  • January 1 to 31: personal property listing
  • August: 2% early payment discount
  • September 1: taxes due
  • January 6: interest begins

Buyers and sellers usually split the bill by closing date, and the attorney's settlement statement should show the split.

faqs.q: What is the Yadkin County tax office phone number?
faqs.a: 336-849-7903. The counter serves walk-ins on weekdays, with the day ending at 5:00 pm.

faqs.q: Does Yadkin County offer an early payment discount?
faqs.a: Yes, a 2% discount applies when taxes are paid in August. Confirm the current terms with the office.

faqs.q: Can I pay Yadkin County taxes by phone?
faqs.a: Yes, call 866-249-4184 and have the year and bill number ready.

faqs.q: When is the Yadkin County revaluation?
faqs.a: A 2027 revaluation is underway. Ask the office when notices will be mailed.

faqs.q: How much is the Yadkin County solid waste fee?
faqs.a: $76.00 per household and $38.00 for households with the elderly exemption, with additional stickers at $10.00.
